title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers

evidence.note: Wikipedia's article states: 'In 1974, The Strange Love of Martha Ivers entered the public domain in the United States because the claimants did not renew its copyright registration in the 28th year after publication.' It cites Pascual 2009, p. 62. This is a secondary claim. No search of any Catalog of Copyright Entries volume or the Copyright Office public catalog was done for this dossier, so non-renewal is not confirmed from a primary record. The print stays undetermined until the renewal records are checked.
evidence.source: Wikipedia, The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (secondary, not a primary record)

evidence.note: Two Internet Archive items exist for the film. The item 'the-strange-love-of-martha-ivers-1946' (uploader RetroFlixUploads, uploaded October 23, 2023) shows the license field https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/. The item 'Martha_Ivers' (uploader jordonz, uploaded April 11, 2008, 115 min) shows the license field http://creativecommons.org/licenses/publicdomain/. These are uploader assertions, not Copyright Office records.

Wikipedia credits the music to Miklós Rózsa. This dossier has not checked the copyright status of the score. The musical composition's copyright and renewal are separate from the film's, and the status of the recorded soundtrack is unsupported here and uncertain.
evidence.source: Wikipedia, The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (secondary; composer credit only)

evidence.note: Wikipedia says the film was adapted from playwright John Patrick's short story 'Love Lies Bleeding'. Wikipedia does not state a publication date or place for the story. The story's publication and renewal history are unchecked, so its copyright term is unknown. The AFI Catalog could not be loaded (HTTP 403), so the credit is not confirmed from it.
evidence.source: Wikipedia, The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (secondary)

evidence.note: Wikipedia lists a Paramount Home Entertainment DVD (October 25, 2002), an HDClassics restored DVD and Blu-ray set (2012), and a Kino Lorber Blu-ray (September 22, 2022) that it describes as a '4K restoration from the original film elements'. These dates and the restoration description come from Wikipedia only. The Kino Lorber product page could not be loaded (HTTP 403), so they are not confirmed against a Kino Lorber or retailer page. A faithful restoration adds no new US copyright. Added material, such as new titles, subtitles, commentary or bonus content, can be protected.
evidence.source: Wikipedia, The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (secondary; not confirmed on a Kino Lorber page)

editorial:
The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (1946) is a Paramount noir directed by Lewis Milestone, with music credited to Miklós Rózsa. Wikipedia says it is adapted from John Patrick's short story 'Love Lies Bleeding'. Three childhood friends share a secret. Years later two of them are married and run the city, and the third comes back. A creator can reach for it for clips, a restored-noir double bill or a score study.

The rights trap is that the print's status rests on one secondary claim. Wikipedia says the copyright was not renewed in the 28th year, so the film entered the US public domain in 1974. No search of a Catalog of Copyright Entries volume or a Copyright Office record was done here, so this is unconfirmed. Check the 1973-1975 volumes yourself before relying on it. Separately, Wikipedia lists a 2022 Kino Lorber Blu-ray as a 4K restoration. We could not confirm that on a Kino Lorber page. A faithful copy of the film adds no new copyright, but a disc's extras, titles and commentary can be protected. The score's composition copyright and the source story's status are separate questions and are also unchecked.
faq: Is The Strange Love of Martha Ivers in the US public domain?

Wikipedia reports that its copyright was not renewed and that it entered the US public domain in 1974. No primary renewal record was searched for this dossier, so the print stays undetermined here. Check the 1973-1975 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes and the Copyright Office public catalog before relying on it. The score and the source story have their own separate copyright status.
Can I use footage from the Kino Lorber 4K restoration?

Do not assume so. A faithful restoration of an out-of-copyright film adds no new US copyright. Added material such as new titles, commentary or bonus features can be protected. Ripping a copy-protected disc can also raise a DMCA anti-circumvention problem under 17 U.S.C. 1201. Confirm the film's status first.
